topic: Responsive Design, Accessibility, and Inclusive UX
learningObjectives: Apply responsive design principles across different screen sizes.
Identify accessibility barriers in common interface patterns.
Apply basic accessibility principles to interface content and controls.
Design inclusive interactions that support diverse user needs.

activities.title: Responsive Layout Explorer
activities.instruction: Adjust the viewport and observe how the interface adapts.

content.concept: Responsive design adapts layout, content, sizing, and interactions to different screen sizes and device contexts.
content.tip: Observe when columns stack, navigation changes, and content resizes.

activities.title: Accessibility Barrier Hunt
activities.instruction: Identify the accessibility problem in each interface example.

content.concept: Accessibility barriers can involve poor contrast, missing labels, keyboard access, unclear focus states, small text, excessive motion, and interaction complexity.
content.tip: Look beyond visual appearance and consider how users with different abilities interact with the interface.

activities.title: Inclusive Pattern Matcher
activities.instruction: Match each accessibility need with an appropriate design solution.

content.concept: Inclusive design provides multiple ways to perceive information, navigate interfaces, and complete tasks.
content.tip: Choose solutions that reduce barriers rather than relying on a single sensory or interaction method.

choices: Color vision deficiency → Color plus text or icons

activities.title: Responsive Interface Builder
activities.instruction: Build a layout that reorganizes appropriately across breakpoints.

content.concept: Responsive interfaces reorganize components and content while preserving usability across different viewport sizes.
content.tip: Think about what should remain visible, what can stack, and what can collapse on smaller screens.

separation.learning: Teach the concept through an interactive experience.
